children: Cheaper oil and improving risk appetite lift the euro, but strong expectations for another Fed hike keep the dollar in contention.
pair traded around $1.1220 early Tuesday, holding most of Monday’s 0.7% advance but still well within the short-term range of $1.1120 to $1.1250.
The recovery reversed Friday’s decline after strong US employment figures boosted the dollar, leaving the pair roughly in the middle of the trading range it has occupied over the past month.

encouraged investors back into riskier assets, reducing demand for the dollar.

Brent crude slipped toward $91.50 a barrel Tuesday, extending Monday’s nearly 6% settlement decline. Cheaper imported energy could ease pressure on household purchasing power and business costs if the decline persists.
European inflation nevertheless remains elevated. Eurozone inflation reached 4% in October, while the ECB held rates unchanged that month.
Policymakers have continued discussing a possible December increase, keeping the European side of the interest-rate equation relevant to the euro-dollar.
Lower oil has competing implications for the currency. It can support Europe’s growth outlook while reducing the need for further monetary tightening.
🏦 US CPI puts the dollar back in charge

October’s US inflation report arrives at 8:30 a.m. ET, with forecasts pointing to monthly increases of 0.3% in headline prices and 0.2% in core prices, which exclude food and energy. The release gives traders a fresh test of whether inflation remains persistent enough to justify further tightening.

Markets already assign roughly an 85% probability to a December Fed hike, following October hiring that exceeded forecasts. That leaves the dollar with substantial interest-rate support despite Monday’s retreat.

Traders now need to watch $1.12 as the immediate round-number reference, with the recent area around $1.115 providing downside context. Holding above $1.12 after the inflation release could strengthen the recovery’s footing.
US CPI data on deck for today

title: EURUSD: Euro Punches Above $1.12 to Test Ceiling. Will US Inflation Spark a Breakout?
